critiques.title: Expose exact monthly velocity values on hover
critiques.issue: The velocity chart shows two lines without hover details, so users cannot read exact completed and target values for a month without estimating from the axis.
critiques.rationale: Analytical monitoring benefits from precise values when users inspect a department's monthly performance against target.
critiques.evidence: The line chart has no encoding.tooltip and the mark has point set to false.
critiques.suggestion: Add a tooltip to task-velocity that exposes month, series, and summed value from the folded line encoding so users can read exact monthly completed versus target values.

critiques.title: Use bars for status comparison instead of slices
critiques.issue: The donut chart makes it harder to compare project-status counts across categories, especially for small differences and filtered department views.
critiques.rationale: Status monitoring is a comparison task; aligned lengths are easier to judge than angles and arc areas, and they remain clearer when counts are small.
critiques.evidence: Project Status Distribution encodes summed value with theta in an arc mark across four statuses.
critiques.suggestion: Convert the donut to a sorted horizontal bar chart with status on one axis and project count on the other.

critiques.title: Order departments by workload size
critiques.issue: The department bars follow source order instead of task volume, so the heaviest-loaded teams are not immediately apparent.
critiques.rationale: A descending sort makes the cross-department ranking readable at a glance and better supports intervention triage.
critiques.evidence: The x encoding has no value-based sort even though tasks is the comparison measure.
critiques.suggestion: Sort departments from highest to lowest task count.

critiques.title: Bring burndown into the department exploration flow
critiques.issue: The department filter and bar-click cross-filter update three views, but the burndown chart remains disconnected, so one quarter of the dashboard does not respond during department-level exploration.
critiques.rationale: If users are comparing delivery health by department, leaving the burndown view static breaks the coordinated reading path and forces them to mentally separate one metric from the rest.
critiques.evidence: The visible department filter targets task-velocity, department-tasks, and project-status only, and the burndown data has no department field to participate.
critiques.suggestion: Either derive burndown by department and wire it into the same department interactions, or replace this tile with a metric that can participate in department comparison.
